body: @jstenback I am looking to make my first contribution ,so i would really appriciate if you allow me to join the next meeting.
@DeftRaj Apologies for missing this comment last week. Can you please send me (jstenback@google.com) an email address and I'll get you added to the next meeting (or whatever week(s) work for you).

Minutes:

- Canvas Text Metrics Edition: Stephen Chenney requested that issue 10677 regarding canvas text metrics for editing and text styling be skipped for the current week. The team received a comment from the Skia team and is awaiting a reply from Apple, so the item will be removed from the agenda and revisited when ready.
- Sanitized Wild Parsing: Noam Rosenthal noted that 12645, concerning sanitized wild parsing, was discussed the previous week and the agenda-plus label was removed.
- Menu Elements: Mason Freed provided an update for issue 11729, requesting additional comments on the menu elements and specification pull requests, on belalf of David Baron.
- Navigation: PR 11765. Keith Cirkel and Noam Rosenthal noted that Ollie and Andreas are currently on vacation, which limits the ability to get the necessary reviews from Mozilla. Consequently, the item will be held until the relevant parties return.
- Input Type Checkbox Switch - Stage Approval: Andres Regalado Rosas requested that the proposal for adding a switch attribute to input type checkbox (issue 4180) be moved to stage one. While Luke and Keith Cirkel discussed whether it should proceed to stage two given that it is shipped in one browser, the group reached a consensus to proceed to stage one for now, as a matching HTML specification pull request and CSS forms specification are preferred before advancing further.
- Input Type Checkbox Switch - Architectural Strategy: During the discussion on the switch attribute, Dan Clark, Luke, Keith Cirkel, and Mason Freed debated whether to utilize an "appearance: base-switch" or a broader "appearance: base" approach for form controls. The group decided to file an issue in the CSS working group drafts repository to resolve the debate regarding the opt-in strategy for these features.
- Platform Provided Behaviors for Custom Elements: Ana Sollano Kim announced updates to the explainer for issue 12150 regarding platform-provided behaviors. The proposal now includes an HTML button behavior that mirrors native button functionality to improve dynamism and composability, following discussions at a hackfest. Ana requested that the team review the changes and plans to provide updates on Matrix before returning to the meeting the following week.
- Declarative Out-of-Order Streaming: Noam Rosenthal updated the group on PR 11818, noting that the agenda-plus label was removed because Ana provided a review before going on leave. While progress is awaiting the return of team members currently on vacation, the PR is not blocked.
- Responsive Iframes Proposal: Noam Rosenthal discussed the status of PR 2444 regarding responsive iframes, highlighting that a meta tag attribute was added to the proposal to allow iframes to opt-in to responsive sizing via an ancestor list. To address security concerns raised by Mozilla regarding cross-origin discovery, the team proposed a structure where the embedder cannot determine if they were rejected. While Luke suggested potential refinements for origin-based permissions and unhyphenated attribute naming, the general sentiment regarding the direction of using the frame ancestor meta tag was positive.
- Spellcheck Custom Dictionary: Brian Kardell requested that issue 12590 be advanced to stage two, noting that although previous feedback was non-committal, there were no explicit objections. Brian addressed concerns regarding internationalization and specific methods, asserting that this proposal is a viable first step. Johnny Stenback and Brian agreed to withhold a decision until key contributors like Olli and Anne return from vacation, at which point the group will seek final input in the pull request.
